design.text: Randomized 2:2:1 to open-label amivantamab plus lazertinib (Arm A), double-blind osimertinib plus matching oral placebo (Arm B, control), or double-blind lazertinib plus oral matching placebo (Arm C); no crossover after progression; stratified by EGFR mutation type, Asian race, and presence of brain metastases.

citations.quote: Eligible patients underwent randomization in a 2:2:1 ratio to receive open label amivantamab in combination with lazertinib (Arm A, n=429), double-blind osimertinib in combination with matching oral placebo (Arm B, control, n=429), or double-blind lazertinib in combination with oral matching placebo (Arm C, n=217).
Stratification factors were *EGFR* mutation type (exon 19 deletion versus L858R substitution), Asian race (yes versus no), and presence of brain metastases (yes vs no).
The protocol did not allow for crossover after disease progression (PD) on study treatment.

population.text: Adult patients with previously untreated locally advanced unresectable or metastatic NSCLC harboring EGFR exon 19 deletions or exon 21 L858R substitution mutations.

citations.quote: MARIPOSA is an ongoing, randomized, multiregional trial that compares the efficacy and safety of amivantamab in combination with lazertinib versus osimertinib as first-line treatment in patients with locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC harboring *EGFR* exon 19 deletions or exon 21 L858R substitution mutations

endpoint.text: Progression-free survival (PFS) assessed by blinded independent central review (BICR) for Arm A compared to Arm B; overall survival was a key secondary endpoint.

citations.quote: The primary endpoint is progression-free survival (PFS) as assessed by blinded independent central review (BICR) for Arm A compared to Arm B. Overall survival (OS) is a key secondary endpoint which is being formally tested with type I error control.

n.text: N=1,074 total randomized: Arm A (amivantamab + lazertinib) n=429, Arm B (osimertinib) n=429, Arm C (lazertinib) n=217.

citations.quote: A total of 1,074 participants were randomly assigned to treatment in a 2:2:1 ratio as indicated in the schema below.

Eligible patients underwent randomization in a 2:2:1 ratio to receive open label amivantamab in combination with lazertinib (Arm A, n=429), double-blind osimertinib in combination with matching oral placebo (Arm B, control, n=429), or double-blind lazertinib in combination with oral matching placebo (Arm C, n=217).

result.text: Met primary endpoint: PFS HR 0.70 (95% CI 0.58, 0.85; p=0.0002) favoring Arm A; median PFS 23.7 months (95% CI 19.1, 27.7) in Arm A vs 16.6 months (95% CI 14.8, 18.5) in Arm B. First interim OS HR 0.81 (95% CI 0.62, 1.06; p=0.120), not statistically significant.

citations.quote: MARIPOSA met its primary endpoint of BICR-assessed PFS with a hazard ratio (HR) of 0.70 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.58, 0.85; p-value = 0.0002) favoring Arm A (amivantamab in combination with lazertinib). The median PFS was 23.7 months (95% CI: 19.1, 27.7) in Arm A and 16.6 months (95% CI: 14.8, 18.5) in Arm B.
The OS HR was 0.81 (95% CI: 0.62, 1.06; p-value = 0.120), which was not statistically significant. The median OS was not reached in either Arms A or B.

indication.text: LAZCLUZE is indicated in combination with amivantamab for the first-line treatment of adult patients with locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC with EGFR exon 19 deletions or exon 21 L858R substitution mutations, as detected by an FDA-approved test.

target_moa.text: Lazertinib is an oral third-generation tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) of EGFR, with activity in NSCLC harboring EGFR exon 19 deletions and exon 21 L858R substitution mutations as well as exon 20 T790M mutations; given with amivantamab, a bispecific antibody binding EGFR and the MET receptor.

citations.quote: Lazertinib (LAZCLUZE) is an oral third-generation tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) of the epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) protein, with activity in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) tumors harboring *EGFR* exon 19 deletions and exon 21 L858R substitution mutations, in addition to exon 20 T790M mutations.
Amivantamab-vmjw (RYBREVANT) is a bispecific antibody that binds to the extracellular domains of EGFR and the mesenchymal-epithelial transition (MET) receptor.

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (>=20%) were rash, nail toxicity, infusion-related reaction (amivantamab), musculoskeletal pain, edema, stomatitis, VTE, paresthesia, fatigue, diarrhea, constipation, COVID-19, hemorrhage, dry skin, decreased appetite, pruritus, nausea, and ocular toxicity. Rash occurred in 86% (Grade 3 or 4 26%) and nail toxicity in 71% (11%). Serious adverse reactions occurred in 49% of patients; fatal adverse reactions in 7%. VTE occurred in 36% of patients (Grade 3 in 10%).

citations.quote: - The most common adverse reactions (\ge 20\%) were rash, nail toxicity, infusion-related reaction (amivantamab), musculoskeletal pain, edema, stomatitis, VTE, paresthesia, fatigue, diarrhea, constipation, COVID-19, hemorrhage, dry skin, decreased appetite, pruritus, nausea, and ocular toxicity. (6.1)

Rash*	86	26	48	1.2
Nail toxicity*	71	11	34	0.7
Serious adverse reactions occurred in 49% of patients who received LAZCLUZE in combination with amivantamab.

Fatal adverse reactions occurred in 7% of patients who received LAZCLUZE in combination with amivantamab due to death not otherwise specified (1.2%); sepsis and respiratory failure (1% each); pneumonia, myocardial infarction, and sudden death (0.7% each); cerebral infarction, pulmonary embolism (PE), and COVID-19 infection (0.5% each); and ILD/pneumonitis, acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), and cardiopulmonary arrest (0.2% each).
In MARIPOSA [see Adverse Reactions (6.1)], VTE occurred in 36% of patients receiving LAZCLUZE in combination with amivantamab, including Grade 3 in 10% and Grade 4 in 0.5% of patients.

detail.text: cobas EGFR Mutation Test v2 used to detect EGFR exon 19 deletions or exon 21 L858R substitution mutations in tumor or plasma specimens.

citations.quote: Among the 858 patients with EGFR exon 19 deletion or L858R substitution mutations that were randomized between the amivantamab plus LAZCLUZE arm versus the osimertinib arm, available tissue samples from 544 (63%) patients had evaluable results when tested retrospectively using the cobas EGFR Mutation Test v2.

Together, the study results support the clinical effectiveness of cobas EGFR Mutation Test v2 for both tissue and plasma to identify patients with EGFR exon 19 deletion and L858R mutations who may benefit from treatment with lazertinib in combination with amivantamab.

requirement.text: 4681-1 Conduct comprehensive safety analyses from clinical studies that further characterize the known serious risk of venous thromboembolic events (VTEs) in patients treated with amivantamab intravenously (IV) and patients treated with amivantamab subcutaneously (SC), in combination with lazertinib. Provide the incidence, timing, and outcome of VTEs by grade in patients who did not receive prophylactic anticoagulation, who received prophylactic anticoagulation for the initial 4 months of study therapy only, who continued prophylactic anticoagulation beyond 4 months of study therapy, and who required initiation of treatment-level anticoagulation. Monitor patients for VTEs throughout study therapy until treatment discontinuation.
